request: I need a revenue dashboard for the board.

questions.question: What decision should the board make with this dashboard? For example: set next year's budget, decide where to invest in marketing, or check if the business is on track.
questions.why: Decision supported is the top priority and is unknown. It shapes the KPIs, comparison and breakdowns.
questions.answer: The board should use it to check whether we're on track: how 2026 revenue and gross margin compare with 2025, by quarter, since they meet quarterly.

questions.question: How should we count revenue? Which orders should be left out? Options: (a) all orders except cancelled ones, (b) all orders except cancelled and returned ones, (c) all orders, whatever their status.
questions.why: Revenue is ambiguous. Order status handling changes both revenue and gross margin.
questions.answer: Option (b). Revenue should be the sale price of items that were neither cancelled nor returned.

questions.question: Besides the quarterly view, should the board be able to break revenue and margin down by anything? Options: product category, department, marketing channel, or no breakdown (just the totals by quarter).
questions.why: Breakdowns not stated. Audience is board, already known.
questions.answer: Yes, please split it by department, Men and Women. Keep the quarterly view as well.

brief.business_question: How do revenue and gross margin in 2026 compare with 2025, by quarter, in total and for Men and Women?
brief.audience: The board of directors, who meet quarterly. Readers are non-technical.
brief.decision_supported: Check whether the business is on track in 2026 compared with 2025.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.plain_definition: Sum of the sale price of order items that were neither cancelled nor returned. Items are assigned to the quarter in which the order was placed. Shown in dollars.

kpis.name: Gross margin (amount)
kpis.plain_definition: Revenue minus the product cost of the same items (neither cancelled nor returned), by quarter.

kpis.name: Gross margin %
kpis.plain_definition: Gross margin amount divided by revenue, for the same items and quarter.

brief.time_range: Q1 2025 to Q3 2026 (data runs to September 2026). 2026 Q4 is not yet available.
brief.comparison: Each 2026 quarter against the same quarter of 2025 (year over year), with absolute and % change.
open_assumptions: Gross margin was not defined by the stakeholder. Assumed: sale price minus product cost, on the same non-cancelled, non-returned items. Please approve.
Quarters are calendar quarters (Jan–Mar, etc.). Please confirm this matches the company's fiscal year.
Items are dated by the order creation date, not shipping or delivery date. Please confirm.
Q3 2026 is assumed to be complete if data runs to the end of September 2026. If September is partial, Q3 will be labelled as partial.
Revenue is shown before any tax or shipping, as only item sale prices are in the data.
Only the Men and Women departments exist in the data and are shown. Totals equal Men plus Women.
Year-to-date 2026 versus the same period of 2025 is shown as a summary, in addition to quarters. This is an addition for approval.
out_of_scope: Full-year 2026 revenue and margin, and Q4 2026: the data ends in September 2026, so these can't be reported. Any full-year figure would be a forecast, which was not requested.
Revenue targets or budget comparison: no target or budget data is available, so 'on track' is judged only against 2025.

mappings.logic: Sum order_items.sale_price for items where order_items.status is not Cancelled and not Returned. That keeps Complete, Shipped and Processing. Grain is one row per item.
For the same items as revenue (status not Cancelled or Returned), sum (order_items.sale_price - products.cost). Equals revenue minus cost. Cost comes from joining each item to its product.

Total gross margin amount divided by total revenue, for the same items and the same quarter or group. Calculate it from the summed amounts. Do not average item-level percentages. Totals and the YTD view must be recalculated from sums, not by adding or averaging quarterly percentages.
Calendar quarter of order_items.created_at (UTC), the date the item was ordered. This is the order placement date at item level and avoids needing the orders table. Group by year and quarter.

Department the product is sold in, from products via order_items.product_id = products.id. Do not use orders.gender or users.gender, which describe the customer. The Total view is Men plus Women, with no department split.
Filter on the year of order_items.created_at. Keep 2025 and 2026 only.
Filter products.department to Men, Women, or no filter for both.

Keep order_items.created_at from 2025-01-01 up to but not including 2026-10-01. The upper bound is needed because item dates run into October 2026. The 2026 quarters Q1 to Q3 are each compared with the same 2025 quarter.

For each quarter (Q1 to Q3), take the 2026 value minus the 2025 value, and that difference divided by the 2025 value. For gross margin %, show the change in percentage points instead. The same comparison is made for Men, Women and Total.
Sum revenue and margin for 1 Jan to 30 Sep 2026 and for 1 Jan to 30 Sep 2025, using the same status rule. Then compare the two.

joins: order_items.product_id = products.id (needed for cost and department; use a left join and check for unmatched items)
order_items.order_id = orders.order_id (optional; only needed if the order's own created_at or status is wanted. Not needed for the KPIs.)

gaps.reason: products.cost is a single current unit cost per product. The data has no history of cost changes. Gross margin is therefore an approximation if costs changed between 2025 and 2026.
gaps.substitute: Use products.cost and label the margin as based on current product cost.

gaps.item: Confirmation that calendar quarters match the fiscal year
gaps.reason: The data has no fiscal calendar. This needs the stakeholder to confirm.

gaps.item: Revenue net of tax and shipping
gaps.reason: The data has no tax, shipping or discount fields other than sale_price. Revenue is item sale price only.
gaps.substitute: Label revenue as item sales before tax and shipping.

gaps.reason: No target or budget data exists.
Data ends in September 2026 (item dates run a few days into October, and are excluded).
gaps.substitute: Year-to-date to September, compared with the same period of 2025.

gaps.reason: Returns and cancellations happen after the order date. Recent orders (especially Q3 2026) still have Shipped or Processing items that may later be returned or cancelled. The data cannot show what will happen to them.
gaps.substitute: Add a note on the dashboard that recent quarters may be overstated. Optionally show the Shipped and Processing share of revenue by quarter.

data_notes: Item status is stored per item and can differ within an order. The brief's rule uses order_items.status, not orders.status. Items from the same order can be counted differently.

Excluding Cancelled and Returned keeps Complete, Shipped and Processing items. Shipped and Processing items are not yet delivered. The stakeholder should confirm they count as revenue. If not, restrict to Complete only.

order_items.created_at runs to 2026-10-04, but orders.created_at stops at 2026-09-30. Filter to before 2026-10-01 so Q3 2026 contains only July to September. Q3 is complete only if data to 30 Sep is fully loaded. The last order is 23:59 on 30 Sep, which suggests it is.

The brief dates items by the order placement date. order_items.created_at is used as that date. It may differ slightly from orders.created_at. Reconcile the two before release. orders has 117,984 rows but order IDs run up to 125,704, so some orders are missing from orders. Joining to orders could drop items, so avoid it for the KPIs.
Department comes from products.department (Men or Women). orders.gender and users.gender are the customer's gender and would give different numbers.
Timestamps are UTC. Quarter boundaries are in UTC, not local time.
products.cost ranges from under $0.01 to about $557. Some very low costs and sale prices (as low as $0.02) may be data quality issues worth a quick check, but they have a small effect on totals.
Personal fields in users (first_name, last_name, email) are not needed and must not be shown.
Gross margin % for Total must be computed from total margin and total revenue. It is not the average of the Men and Women percentages.

audit.summary: Two findings could change the numbers: items with zero or negative prices (1), and items whose product is missing from the product list (2). Both involve only 5 rows, so the effect is small, but they should be excluded and counted. The date-order problems (3, 4, 5) and the category spelling problem (6) are real data errors, but they don't touch any KPI as long as we use the order creation date, item status and department.

issues.explanation: Five items have a price of zero or below. A price cannot be negative for a normal sale. Negative values would reduce revenue and margin. A zero price may be a free gift or an error. The amounts are small, but they are wrong for a 'sum of sale prices' measure.
issues.proposed_rule: Exclude order items with sale_price <= 0 from Revenue and Gross margin. Log the count and value excluded in the pipeline notes.
issues.decision_question: Are negative or zero prices refunds, adjustments or free gifts? We propose to leave them out of revenue. Do you agree?

issues.explanation: Five order items point to products that do not exist in the product list (ids 30001-30005). We have no cost and no department for them. Margin cannot be calculated, and they cannot be placed in Men or Women. Including their revenue would break the rule that the total equals Men plus Women.
issues.proposed_rule: Exclude order items whose product_id is not found in products.id from all KPIs, so the total equals Men plus Women. Report the number of excluded items and their sale value as a footnote or in the pipeline notes.
issues.decision_question: These 5 items have no product record, so we cannot show their margin or department. Is it fine to leave them out of all figures? Or can the product list be fixed?
issues.rule: every order_items.product_id must exist in products.id

issues.explanation: About 34,000 items show a ship time before the order was placed. That is impossible, so the timestamps are unreliable. The KPIs do not use ship dates. They use the order creation date, so the numbers are not affected unless the creation date itself is wrong. If it is wrong, a few items near quarter ends could land in the wrong quarter.
issues.proposed_rule: Do not use shipped_at in any KPI. Use created_at for quarter assignment. Do not delete these rows. Flag shipped_at as unreliable for any future shipping metric.
issues.rule: shipped_at must not be before created_at

issues.explanation: About 5,800 items show a delivery time before the order was placed. This is impossible. Delivery dates are not used in this dashboard, so the KPIs are not affected.
issues.proposed_rule: Do not use delivered_at in any KPI. Keep the rows. Flag delivered_at as unreliable for any future delivery-time metric.
issues.rule: delivered_at must not be before created_at

issues.explanation: 637 returned items have a return time before the order time. The dates are wrong, but the KPIs only need to know whether an item was returned, not when. Some samples sit right at a quarter boundary. This could mean the creation date is slightly off, but that cannot be confirmed.
issues.proposed_rule: Identify returned items by item status (Returned) only, or returned_at is not null if status is missing. Do not use returned_at timing. Keep these rows excluded as returned. Assign quarter by created_at.
issues.rule: returned_at must not be before created_at

issues.explanation: Five products have category names with spelling, case or spacing variants, such as 'jeans ' and 'Accesories'. The dashboard splits by department, not category, so no KPI is affected. It would split category counts if we added a category view later.
issues.proposed_rule: Trim spaces, then map variants: JEANS and 'jeans ' to Jeans, 'Tops and Tees' to 'Tops & Tees', Sweater to Sweaters, Accesories to Accessories. Do not change department values.
issues.rule: rare spellings of a common value: 'JEANS' looks like 'Jeans'; 'jeans ' looks like 'Jeans'; 'Tops and Tees' looks like 'Tops & Tees'; 'Sweater' looks like 'Sweaters'; 'Accesories' looks like 'Accessories'

time_window.explanation: Q1 2025 to Q3 2026, using calendar quarters in UTC. Items are placed by order_items.created_at. Q4 2026 and full-year 2026 are left out because the data ends on 2026-09-30. Item dates run into early October 2026, so those rows are cut off at 2026-09-30 23:59:59.

shared_rules: Base table is order_items. Join each item to products on order_items.product_id = products.id to get cost and department.

Count only items whose status is not 'Cancelled' and not 'Returned'. That keeps Complete, Shipped and Processing. If status is missing, treat the item as returned when returned_at is not null. Do not use the timing of returned_at, shipped_at or delivered_at.
Exclude items with sale_price <= 0 (5 items). Log their count and value in the pipeline notes.
Exclude items with no matching product record (product_id 30001-30005, 5 items). Log their count and value in the pipeline notes. This keeps Total equal to Men plus Women.
Place each item in a quarter by order_items.created_at (UTC). Keep 2025-01-01 up to but not including 2026-10-01. Quarters are calendar quarters: Q1 Jan-Mar, Q2 Apr-Jun, Q3 Jul-Sep.
Department comes from products.department (Men or Women). Never use the customer's gender from orders or users.
Do not join to orders. Do not show any personal fields.
The Total row is computed from summed Men plus Women amounts. Ratios are always computed from summed amounts, never by averaging or adding percentages.
Year-over-year change compares each 2026 period with the same period of 2025. Absolute change is 2026 minus 2025. % change is the absolute change divided by the 2025 value.
Amounts are in US dollars, rounded for display only. Do not round before calculating ratios.

Label on the dashboard: revenue is item sales before tax and shipping. Margin uses each product's current cost, not the cost at the time of sale. Recent quarters, especially Q3 2026, may be overstated because Shipped and Processing items can still be returned or cancelled.

metrics.name: Revenue
metrics.question_answered: How much did we sell in each quarter of 2026 compared with the same quarter of 2025, in total and for Men and Women?
metrics.formula: Sum of order_items.sale_price for items that pass the shared rules (status not Cancelled or Returned, sale_price > 0, product found). YoY absolute change = 2026 revenue minus 2025 revenue. YoY % change = absolute change divided by 2025 revenue.
metrics.grain: One row per period (Q1, Q2, Q3 and Jan-Sep year-to-date) x year (2025, 2026) x department view (Men, Women, Total). That is 24 rows. The YoY columns are filled on the 2026 rows.
metrics.time_logic: Quarter from order_items.created_at (UTC). Quarters run Q1 2025 to Q3 2026. Year-to-date is 2025-01-01 to 2025-09-30 against 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-30.
cleaning_rules: If a department and quarter has no qualifying items, revenue is 0. If the 2025 value is 0, show the YoY % change as 'n/a', not a number.
metrics.excluded_example: A 2026 Q2 item with status Returned and a sale price of $60 is not counted. Neither is an item dated 2026-10-02.

metrics.name: Gross margin (amount)
metrics.question_answered: How many dollars of profit on product cost did we make in each quarter of 2026 compared with 2025, in total and for Men and Women?
metrics.formula: Sum of (order_items.sale_price minus products.cost) for the same items as Revenue. This equals Revenue minus product cost. YoY absolute change = 2026 margin minus 2025 margin. YoY % change = absolute change divided by 2025 margin amount.
metrics.grain: One row per period (Q1, Q2, Q3 and Jan-Sep year-to-date) x year (2025, 2026) x department view (Men, Women, Total). That is 24 rows. The YoY columns are filled on the 2026 rows.
metrics.time_logic: Quarter from order_items.created_at (UTC). Quarters run Q1 2025 to Q3 2026. Year-to-date is 2025-01-01 to 2025-09-30 against 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-30.
cleaning_rules: Use the same item set as Revenue, so margin and revenue always match row for row.
Skip any item with a missing cost from both Revenue and margin, so the two stay consistent. Log the count.
If the 2025 margin is 0 or less, show the YoY % change as 'n/a'. Still show the absolute change.
metrics.excluded_example: An item with a product_id that has no product record (for example 30003) is left out, because it has no cost and no department.

metrics.name: Gross margin %
metrics.question_answered: What share of revenue is left after product cost in each quarter, and did it improve or fall compared with 2025?
metrics.formula: Gross margin amount divided by Revenue, both summed over the same items, quarter and department view. YoY change is shown in percentage points: 2026 margin % minus 2025 margin %. Total and year-to-date are recalculated from summed amounts.
metrics.grain: One row per period (Q1, Q2, Q3 and Jan-Sep year-to-date) x year (2025, 2026) x department view (Men, Women, Total). That is 24 rows. The YoY change in percentage points is filled on the 2026 rows.
metrics.time_logic: Quarter from order_items.created_at (UTC). Quarters run Q1 2025 to Q3 2026. Year-to-date is 2025-01-01 to 2025-09-30 against 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-30.
cleaning_rules: Never average item-level or quarterly percentages.
If revenue is 0 for a row, leave the margin % empty and label it 'no sales'. Do not show 0%. Leave the YoY point change empty if either year is 'no sales'.
metrics.excluded_example: A Processing item is kept, but a Cancelled item is excluded from both the margin amount and the revenue in the ratio.

decisions_assumed: Shipped and Processing items count as revenue. Only Cancelled and Returned are excluded, as in the brief. Because these items can still be returned, Q3 2026 may be slightly overstated. A note is shown. If you prefer Complete only, the figures will fall, most for the latest quarter.
Items with a sale price of zero or below (5 items) are left out of revenue and margin. They are treated as errors or non-sales.
The 5 items with no product record (ids 30001-30005) are left out of all figures, so Total equals Men plus Women. The count and value are reported in a footnote.
Gross margin is sale price minus the product's current cost, because the data has no cost history. It is labelled as based on current cost.
Quarters are calendar quarters (Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep). Please confirm this matches the fiscal year.
Items are dated by order_items.created_at in UTC, used as the order date. Orders are not joined, because some orders are missing from the orders table.
Q3 2026 is treated as complete because the last order is at 23:59 on 30 Sep 2026.
Revenue is item sales before tax and shipping. The data has no tax, shipping or discount fields.
A year-to-date view (Jan-Sep 2026 vs Jan-Sep 2025) is added as a summary. Please approve or remove it.
Gross margin % change is shown in percentage points, not as a % change.
Where there is nothing to divide by: margin % shows 'no sales' when revenue is 0. YoY % change shows 'n/a' when the 2025 base is 0 or, for margin, 0 or less.
Shipped, delivered and returned dates are unreliable and are not used. Returned items are identified by status.
Product category spelling fixes are not needed here, because the dashboard uses department only.

sql.sql:
WITH items AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) AS yr,
    CONCAT('Q', CAST(EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM oi.created_at) AS STRING)) AS qtr,
    p.department,
    oi.sale_price
  FROM `analyst-agent-512103.thelook_dirty.order_items` AS oi
  JOIN `analyst-agent-512103.thelook_dirty.products` AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.id
  WHERE oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP('2025-01-01')
    AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP('2026-10-01')
    AND EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM oi.created_at) <= 3
    AND oi.sale_price > 0
    AND NOT (oi.status IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') OR (oi.status IS NULL AND oi.returned_at IS NOT NULL))
    AND p.department IN ('Men', 'Women')
),
item_periods AS (
  SELECT yr, period, department, sale_price
  FROM items, UNNEST([qtr, 'YTD']) AS period
),
scaffold AS (
  SELECT period, yr, department
  FROM UNNEST(['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'YTD']) AS period
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST([2025, 2026]) AS yr
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(['Men', 'Women']) AS department
),
dept_rev AS (
  SELECT s.period, s.yr, s.department,
         COALESCE(SUM(ip.sale_price), 0) AS revenue
  FROM scaffold s
  LEFT JOIN item_periods ip
    ON ip.period = s.period AND ip.yr = s.yr AND ip.department = s.department
  GROUP BY s.period, s.yr, s.department
),
all_rows AS (
  SELECT period, yr, department AS department_view, revenue FROM dept_rev
  UNION ALL
  SELECT period, yr, 'Total' AS department_view, SUM(revenue) AS revenue
  FROM dept_rev
  GROUP BY period, yr
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    cur.period,
    cur.yr AS year,
    cur.department_view,
    cur.revenue,
    IF(cur.yr = 2026, prev.revenue, NULL) AS prior_year_revenue
  FROM all_rows cur
  LEFT JOIN all_rows prev
    ON prev.period = cur.period
   AND prev.department_view = cur.department_view
   AND prev.yr = cur.yr - 1
)
SELECT
  period,
  year,
  department_view,
  revenue,
  prior_year_revenue,
  IF(year = 2026, revenue - prior_year_revenue, NULL) AS yoy_change,
  IF(year = 2026, SAFE_DIVIDE(revenue - prior_year_revenue, NULLIF(prior_year_revenue, 0)), NULL) AS yoy_pct_change,
  CASE
    WHEN year <> 2026 THEN NULL
    WHEN prior_year_revenue = 0 THEN 'n/a'
    ELSE CAST(ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(revenue - prior_year_revenue, prior_year_revenue), 4) AS STRING)
  END AS yoy_pct_change_label
FROM joined
ORDER BY
  CASE period WHEN 'Q1' THEN 1 WHEN 'Q2' THEN 2 WHEN 'Q3' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END,
  year,
  CASE department_view WHEN 'Men' THEN 1 WHEN 'Women' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

sanity_checks.blank_allowed_because: Prior-year revenue is only shown on the 2026 rows. 2025 rows have no prior year in scope.
YoY is only filled on 2026 rows. 2025 rows are the baseline.
Blank on 2025 rows, and when 2025 revenue is 0 (shown as 'n/a' in the label column).

spec.notes: 24 rows: 4 periods (Q1, Q2, Q3, Jan-Sep YTD) x 2 years x (Men, Women, Total). Rules applied: status not Cancelled/Returned (missing status with returned_at set is treated as returned), sale_price > 0, inner join to products (drops items with no product), department from products.department, items placed by order_items.created_at in UTC, window 2025-01-01 to before 2026-10-01, Q1-Q3 only. Total is Men plus Women summed. Empty department-quarter gives revenue 0. If the 2025 value is 0, yoy_pct_change is blank and yoy_pct_change_label is 'n/a'. yoy_pct_change is a fraction (0.10 = 10%). Not joined to orders, no personal fields. The counts and values of excluded items (sale_price <= 0 and items with no product) are not output by this query. They need a separate pipeline log. Dashboard label: revenue is item sales before tax and shipping. Q3 2026 may be overstated because Shipped and Processing items can still be returned or cancelled.

  IF(year = 2026, revenue - prior_year_revenue, NULL) AS yoy_change,
  IF(year = 2026, SAFE_DIVIDE(revenue - prior_year_revenue, NULLIF(prior_year_revenue, 0)), NULL) AS yoy_pct_change,
  CASE
    WHEN year <> 2026 THEN NULL

FROM joined
ORDER BY
  CASE period WHEN 'Q1' THEN 1 WHEN 'Q2' THEN 2 WHEN 'Q3' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END,

WITH items AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) AS year,
    CONCAT('Q', CAST(EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM oi.created_at) AS STRING)) AS quarter_label,
    p.department AS department,
    oi.sale_price AS revenue,
    oi.sale_price - p.cost AS margin
  FROM `analyst-agent-512103.thelook_dirty.order_items` AS oi
  JOIN `analyst-agent-512103.thelook_dirty.products` AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.id
  WHERE oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP('2025-01-01')
    AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP('2026-10-01')
    AND oi.sale_price > 0
    AND p.department IN ('Men', 'Women')
    AND (
      LOWER(TRIM(oi.status)) IN ('complete', 'shipped', 'processing')
      OR (oi.status IS NULL AND oi.returned_at IS NULL)
    )
),
expanded AS (
  SELECT i.year, period, dept_view, i.revenue, i.margin
  FROM items AS i,
    UNNEST([i.quarter_label, 'YTD']) AS period,
    UNNEST([i.department, 'Total']) AS dept_view
),
agg AS (
  SELECT year, period, dept_view,
    SUM(revenue) AS revenue,
    SUM(margin) AS gross_margin_amount
  FROM expanded
  GROUP BY year, period, dept_view
),
skeleton AS (
  SELECT period, year, dept_view
  FROM UNNEST(['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'YTD']) AS period,
    UNNEST([2025, 2026]) AS year,
    UNNEST(['Men', 'Women', 'Total']) AS dept_view
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    s.period, s.year, s.dept_view,
    COALESCE(a.revenue, 0) AS revenue,
    COALESCE(a.gross_margin_amount, 0) AS gross_margin_amount
  FROM skeleton AS s
  LEFT JOIN agg AS a
    ON a.period = s.period AND a.year = s.year AND a.dept_view = s.dept_view
),
with_pct AS (
  SELECT *,
    IF(revenue > 0, SAFE_DIVIDE(gross_margin_amount, revenue), NULL) AS gross_margin_pct
  FROM joined
)
SELECT
  period,
  year,
  dept_view AS department_view,
  revenue,
  gross_margin_amount,
  gross_margin_pct,
  IF(revenue > 0, NULL, 'no sales') AS margin_label,
  IF(year = 2026,
     (gross_margin_pct - MAX(IF(year = 2025, gross_margin_pct, NULL)) OVER (PARTITION BY period, dept_view)) * 100,

headline.label: Revenue growth, Jan–Sep 2026 vs Jan–Sep 2025
headline.context: Men and Women combined. Items not cancelled or returned. Before tax and shipping.

charts.title: Revenue is well above 2025 in every quarter

charts.title: Growth speeds up each quarter, Women slightly ahead
charts.subtitle: Revenue change versus the same quarter of 2025, by department

charts.title: Gross margin dollars grew along with revenue

charts.title: Margin rate is flat at about 52%
charts.subtitle: Gross margin as a share of revenue, Men and Women combined, by quarter

findings: Yes, the business is well ahead of 2025: revenue for Jan–Sep 2026 was $2,341,715, up 80.8% from $1,295,037 in the same months of 2025.
Growth sped up through the year: revenue rose 60.2% in Q1, 72.8% in Q2 and 104.6% in Q3, when it reached $982,311 against $480,025.
Women grew faster than Men in Q3, up 113.6% against 96.8%, and both departments were up strongly in every quarter.
Gross margin dollars rose 81.1% for Jan–Sep, to $1,217,038 from $672,160, but the margin rate stayed near 52%, at 51.8% in Q3 2026 against 52.0% in Q3 2025 (down 0.2 points).

Read with care: margin uses each product's current cost, since past costs are not in the data. Q3 2026 may be slightly high because some recent items can still be returned. The Jan–Sep margin rate change versus 2025 could not be reliably compared, so only quarterly rates are shown. No targets exist, so 'on track' is judged against 2025 only.
